subject: Availability SLAs, ops cost sharing, and proposed timeline

Subject: Availability SLAs and ops cost sharing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with latency and the autoscaling behavior. We're now scoping the commercial ask with procurement: core question is how Redwood models availability commitments and whether operational (oncall/DR) costs can be shared for our high-availability profile.

High-level asks from Acme:
- Target uptime: 99.95% across US regions (sometimes burst to eu)
- Response windows: P1 30 minutes, P2 4 hours, follow-on escalation to our SRE on-call
- Want to understand options for reduced unit pricing if we commit to a 12–18 month consumption band
- Curious if you can offer a cost-share on the dedicated DR pool and an oncall overflow model (we want a sensible split for edge-hours)

Procurement timeline: we'd like a commercial view and an internal estimate by EOD Dec 15 so we can present to our CFO the following week. Can you share a sketch of pricing tiers and any examples of how you split ops costs with similar customers?

If helpful, Samir is our procurement lead and will follow up on contract language.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Systems

Maya — great to hear the demo landed well. Appreciate the clear asks. High level response below; I'll follow with a short proposal (attached) and a spreadsheet showing commit scenarios.

Quick sketch of options that match what you outlined:
1) Uptime tiers (examples)
   - Standard: 99.9% (included with hosted plan) — baseline unit price
   - High-availability: 99.95% — (+x% per token / reserved pool)
   - Premium: 99.99% — (+y%; includes faster oncall escalation and regional failover pool)

2) Response windows and escalation
   - P1 (service-down): 30 minutes response, engineer assigned within 1 hour, escalation to L2 within 4 hours for Premium
   - P2 (partial degradation): 4 hours response, triage next-business-day for Standard

3) Ops cost sharing options (we've done both models for other customers):
   A) Dedicated DR pool paid by customer, with Redwood-operated standby (preferred for isolated workloads)
   B) Shared DR pool: Redwood operates a smaller shared pool; costs split based on committed baseline usage. Example split: 60% customer / 40% Redwood for co-funded standby during business hours; 50/50 for off-hours if your team wants reduced oncall burden.

4) Pricing/discounts tied to commit
   - 12 month commit: staged discount (5–15%) depending on tier and avg monthly tokens
   - 18 month commit: additional 5% step if you hit volume thresholds

I'll attach two files: availability-pricing-v1.pdf (high-level quote + sample SLO language) and commit-scenarios.xlsx (breakouts). A few internal notes cc'd to Ben and Laura on anchoring and concessions.

Next steps I propose:
- We finalize a mutual action plan with milestones to sign (I can draft a MAP and send a DocuSign-ready file)
- If you want a cost-split worked into the SOW we can model a 3-way line item for the DR pool and an onboarding credit in month 1

I'll aim to get a refined number by EOD Monday (Dec 14) so you have buffer ahead of your 15th deadline.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Availability SLAs and ops cost sharing

Quick internal — copying my thoughts into the thread so Priyom can send a clean version to Acme: 

- Anchor the 99.95 tier at a single blended uplift (call it +12% on hosted price) and show a line-item for the DR pool that can be split.
- Offer an onboarding credit (waive first month of the DR pool) if they sign 12 months and hit a $XXk minimum ARR. That preserves economics but buys them the margin.
- Recommend we include a documented runbook access clause (read-only to their SREs) and one annual DR test included in Premium. That reduces friction on procurement.
- For escalation coverage: propose Redwood provide 24/7 L1 triage and business-hours L2; for full L2 24/7 add a surcharge or require a higher commit.

If you want I can sketch concrete numbers in the spreadsheet; otherwise Priyom can surface a single-slide summary for Maya.

—Ben
Director, Commercial Operations
redwood.ai

Thanks Priyom and Ben — that level of detail is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before I present to procurement/CFO: 

- Retroactive credits: if we hit a shortfall (e.g., an incident that causes a hit to availability), are credits applied monthly or quarterly? We prefer monthly so our CFO can model cashflow.
- DR pool split: can you show a worked example for an estimated monthly $30k DR pool (how would 60/40 vs 50/50 impact monthly costs for Acme)?
- Runbook and DR tests: appreciated — can we request one additional paid DR exercise (at a discounted rate) in year 1?
- Timeline constraint: procurement wants a marked-up SOW + sample DocuSign by COB Dec 17 or we push internal review to next month.

If you can get a worked example and a DocuSign-ready MAP by COB Dec 17 that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Maya
